summary: This benchmark evaluates Qwen2.5-Coder-7B against Qwen2.5-14B on 256 Python delimiter repair triplets (768 total prompts) as a qualification gate for cross-model layer transplantation. The 7B coder significantly outperforms the 14B general model, which exhibits a degenerate response bias towards colons under the fill-in-the-middle evaluation format. While the benchmark is tightly scoped and the baseline comparison is skewed by differing pretraining objectives, the methodology is statistically precise, preregistered, and transparently bounded.
strengths: Rigorous statistical reporting, including exact candidate token counts, whole-triplet success metrics, and paired confidence intervals (19.14 pp, 95% CI: 14.45–23.83).
Transparent self-assessment of confounding factors, explicitly bounding findings by noting differences in pretraining data, model size, and response bias.

Well-formulated preregistered qualification gate criteria (requiring >=25 donor-only solves, a 10 pp net margin, and positive lower confidence bound) designed to justify subsequent modular surgery experiments.
Includes explicit references to audit scripts, verification data, and underlying execution hardware.
weaknesses: Asymmetric baseline comparison: Qwen2.5-14B exhibits extreme bias (predicting a colon on 762/768 prompts), largely because general-purpose base LLMs lack fill-in-the-middle (FIM) training, making the 14B model an uncompetitive baseline.
Very narrow task scope restricted to 4 single-token candidates (parenthesis, bracket, brace, colon) in Python syntax repair without testing alternative prompting formats or multi-token generations.
Short submission length (542 words) that reads primarily as an internal qualification report rather than a standalone comprehensive benchmark.
suggestions: Evaluate an instruction-tuned or few-shot prompted version of Qwen2.5-14B to determine whether the colon bias can be mitigated without weight surgery.
Broaden the benchmark to include other coding vs. general model pairs (such as Llama 3 or DeepSeek) to test whether the donor advantage generalizes across architectures.
Include execution latency and memory footprint comparisons alongside logit accuracy when testing on unified memory architectures like Apple Silicon.

claims.text: The difference was 19.14 percentage points (95% paired interval 14.45–23.83).
Bavarian et al. established the method of fill-in-the-middle training in arXiv:2207.14255.
The scoring ran on the owner's Apple M5 Ultra in original model precision.
Qwen2.5-Coder-7B and Qwen2.5-14B are published open-weight model checkpoints.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Efficient Training of Language Models to Fill in the Middle
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Applies fill-in-the-middle logit evaluation to paired Python delimiter triplets specifically as a qualification gate for modular neural layer grafting.
